consensus_summary: The biblical fool primarily symbolizes moral and spiritual rebellion or practical godlessness—one who rejects divine wisdom, despises instruction, and lives as if God does not matter—rather than intellectual deficiency.
book_summary: One who hears God's word and will not do it — the lawless, not the unintelligent.
consensus_core_identification: morally/spiritually rebellious rejecter of God or divine wisdom (not unintelligent)
book_core_identification: hearer of God's word who will not do it (the lawless, not unintelligent)
rationale: Both cores identify the fool as a moral-spiritual category of rebellion/disobedience to God rather than low intelligence. The book's concise phrasing is drawn from the same central texts (Ps 14:1 for godless lawlessness; Matt 7:26 for hearing without doing) that form the consensus primary basis; wording differences are immaterial.
strongest_objection: One could claim the book's focus on 'hears and will not do' slightly privileges the Matt 7:26 case over pure practical atheism or Proverbs gradations, yet consensus itself unifies these under the identical moral core and cites the identical verses.
